# AI / Expert Quickstart

**Example status — excerpt:** blocks are terse API reminders. The tested
end-to-end contract is [Getting Started](getting-started.qmd).

This is a compact map for readers who already know Python, PyTorch, and
Lightning. It summarizes the public path and links to the pages that own each
contract. For a runnable build-to-prediction example, use
[Getting Started](getting-started.qmd).

## Construct A Schema

Use top-level exports through `import json2vec as jv`:

```{python .marimo}
#| echo: true
#| output: true

import torch

import json2vec as jv

model = jv.Model(
    name="order",
    d_model=64,
    n_layers=2,
    n_heads=4,
    batch_size=32,
    embed=True,
    optimizer=lambda module: torch.optim.AdamW(module.parameters(), lr=1e-3),
    customer_tier=jv.Category(size=16),
    line_items=jv.Branch(
        length=32,
        overflow="tail",
        sku=jv.Category(size=2048),
        quantity=jv.Number,
        price=jv.Number,
    ),
    returned=jv.Category(target=True, size=2),
)

model
```

The generated root is named `record` unless `name=...` overrides it. A child
`Branch(length=...)` adds a repeated context. Only leaf tensorfields bind source
values; branches define model structure and alignment.

Configured `topk` values must be integers greater than 1 and strictly less than
Category `size`; binary categories therefore need no separate top-k list.
Category capacity counts content labels only—do not reserve an extra slot for
unavailable content.

## Match The Input Shape

The schema above reads records shaped like:

```{python .marimo}
#| echo: true
#| output: true

record = {
    "customer_tier": "gold",
    "line_items": [
        {"sku": "ABC-123", "quantity": 2, "price": 19.99},
        {"sku": "XYZ-999", "quantity": 1, "price": 7.50},
    ],
    "returned": "false",
}
```

Same-named fields infer queries such as `[*].customer_tier` and
`[*].line_items[*].sku`. Use an explicit `query=...` for stable source-path
differences and a `@jv.preprocess` object for Python logic, normalization,
sorting, or windowing. See [Binding Data](core-concepts/binding-data.qmd) and
[Advanced Query Paths](core-concepts/querypaths.qmd).

## Assign Learning Roles

| Configuration | Input behavior | Output / learning behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| plain leaf | visible when present | context only by default |
| `target=True` | always hidden | supervised decode and loss |
| `p_mask=x` | sampled positions hidden | reconstruction at selected positions |
| `p_prune=x` | whole leaf instances sampled and hidden | reconstruction of the pruned field |
| branch `mask=jv.Mask(...)` | descendant sampling is limited to candidate coordinates/windows | each descendant samples independently within those candidates |
| `embed=True` | does not hide input | exports an embedding at the address |
| `active=False` | excluded from execution | remains in the serializable schema |

`target=True` is shorthand for `p_prune=1.0`. See
[Learning Modes & Embeddings](core-concepts/embeddings.qmd) for the canonical
role definitions and [Dynamic Masking](core-concepts/dynamic-masking.qmd) for
repeated-window selection.

## Run The Lifecycle

JSON2Vec uses ordinary Lightning loops for training and large-batch prediction:

```python
datamodule = jv.PolarsDataModule(
    model=model,
    train=train_frame,
    validate=validate_frame,
    num_workers=0,
    persistent_workers=False,
    pin_memory=False,
)

trainer.fit(model=model, datamodule=datamodule)
metrics = trainer.validate(model=model, datamodule=datamodule)

model.save("model.pt")
restored = jv.Model.load("model.pt")

predictions = restored.predict(
    [{"customer_tier": "gold", "line_items": []}]
)
```

Prediction requests normally omit fields configured with `target=True`. Output
is keyed by `jv.Address`; decoded leaves include `state`, type-specific
`content`, and `inferred`, while configured nodes can include `embedding`.

Use [Training With Lightning](guides/lightning.qmd) for trainer behavior,
[Data Modules](guides/data-modules.qmd) for ingestion, and
[Evaluation And Metrics](guides/evaluation.qmd) for model selection. Use
[Model Lifecycle](guides/model-lifecycle.qmd) for artifact and resume contracts,
and [Batch Inference](guides/batch-inference.qmd) for `jv.Writer` and
rank-partitioned Parquet output.

## Shape The Boundaries

A preprocessor is part of the input contract:

```python
@jv.preprocess
def normalize_order(record: dict) -> jv.Observation:
    return jv.Observation(
        {
            "customer_tier": record["tier"].strip().lower(),
            "line_items": record["items"],
        }
    )

raw_requests = [{"tier": " Gold ", "items": []}]
predictions = restored.predict(raw_requests, preprocess=normalize_order)
```

A postprocessor is part of the application output contract:

```python
@jv.postprocess
def response(predictions):
    field = predictions[jv.Address("order", "returned")]
    return {"returned": field["content"]["value"]}
```

Pass the same preprocessor through training and inference. Keep the stable,
address-keyed model output intact until the postprocessor boundary. See
[Data Flow](core-concepts/data-flow.qmd) and
[Postprocessors](guides/postprocessors.qmd).

## Public API Map

| Need | Public surface | Authoritative page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Root model | `jv.Model(...)` | [Model Tree](core-concepts/model-tree.qmd) |
| Repeated context | `jv.Branch(...)` | [Branch](data-types/branch.qmd) |
| Typed leaves | `jv.Number`, `Category`, `Set`, `Entity`, `DateParts`, `Boolean`, `Vector`, `Text` | [Built-In Data Types](core-concepts/data-types.qmd) |
| In-memory / streaming input | `jv.PolarsDataModule`, `jv.StreamingDataModule` | [Data Modules](guides/data-modules.qmd) |
| Interactive prediction | `model.predict(...)` | [Getting Started](getting-started.qmd#interpret-the-prediction) |
| Prediction contract | address-keyed `state`, `content`, `inferred`, `embedding` | [Prediction Output](guides/prediction-output.qmd) |
| Batch prediction | `jv.Writer(...)` | [Batch Inference](guides/batch-inference.qmd) |
| Online prediction | `jv.Deployment(...)` | [Serving](guides/serving.qmd) |
| Input / output transforms | `@jv.preprocess`, `@jv.postprocess` | [Binding Data](core-concepts/binding-data.qmd), [Postprocessors](guides/postprocessors.qmd) |
| Schema selection / mutation | `jv.where(...)`, `update`, `extend`, `delete`, `reset`, `override` | [Model Tree](core-concepts/model-tree.qmd#schema-roles-and-mutations) |

## Contract Checklist

- Name the root with `Model(name=...)`; use child `Branch(length=...)` for
  repeated data.
- Keep `n_heads` positive and even. For the root, every Branch, and each leaf
  using `pooling="query"`, require `d_model % n_heads == 0` and
  `d_model // n_heads >= 2`.
- Put `Entity` under a repeated context and do not assume its local indices
  align across observations or sibling leaves.
- Set bounded capacity for Category and Set fields, then monitor vocabulary
  growth rather than inventing a missing-value class.
- Use `overflow="tail"` only when source order places the newest values last.
- Include targets in train/validation data; omit them from ordinary prediction
  requests.
- Preserve the same preprocessing, schema, vocabulary/normalizer state, and
  weights across evaluation and inference.
